doc: Floor materials for the tier-1 physics layer (docs/design/TIER1_PHYSICS.md 4.5; read through props.floor_props and forces). impact_hardness, scratch and mu are manipulation's FLOOR_HARDNESS, FLOOR_SCRATCH and FLOOR_FRICTION unchanged; c_rr and the water columns are added. A room's floor is its floor_<room> entity's material, else the room's floor_material, else its terrain, else `default`; a rug under the cell turns a hard floor into `rug`.

columns.impact_hardness: how hard a landing is, tile = 1.0 (effective drop height = height x hardness / padding); on a soft floor, the compacted layer's once its cushion has bottomed out
columns.cushion_m: soft floors: depth of the layer that stops a falling item before it bottoms out (pile and pad, thatch and topsoil); the drop tolerances are drops onto tile, where an item stops within about 1 mm, so while the cushion works the effective drop is h x 1 mm / (1 mm + cushion_m). null: a hard floor
columns.cushion_j: soft floors: impact energy the cushion takes under a small item before it bottoms out (J); the energy beyond it lands with impact_hardness. Light things (an egg, a mug) are stopped by the cushion, heavy ones bottom it out (impact.effective_drop_m)
columns.mu: static friction of a wood or plastic furniture foot on this floor
columns.c_rr: rolling resistance of casters, wheels and balls
columns.soft: a soft floor (carpet, turf): sliders need their soft-floor factor and a rug adds nothing
columns.absorbs: liquid soaks in instead of standing as a puddle
columns.film_mm: puddle film thickness on this floor, mm (null: the liquid's own film on a hard floor)
columns.water_tolerance_s: standing water this long damages the floor (null: unlimited)
columns.water_damage: the damage kind standing water causes

tile.source: glazed ceramic or porcelain tile: rigid, glaze resists scratching; c_rr about 0.01 for hard casters

stone.source: granite, slate and limestone flooring and patios

concrete.source: bare or sealed concrete (garage, basement, driveway): nothing a household drag can scratch

marble.source: polished marble: soft calcite (Mohs 3) shows scratches readily

hardwood.source: site-finished oak or maple with polyurethane: scratches most easily; standing water for about an hour lifts the finish and cups boards

hardwood_unsealed.source: oiled or worn unsealed hardwood: water marks within minutes

laminate.source: laminate planks: HDF core swells at the joints after about 30 min of standing water

vinyl.source: sheet vinyl and luxury vinyl plank: waterproof, slightly cushioned

wood.source: deck, porch and shed boards: weathered outdoor wood

rubber.source: gym rubber flooring: cushions drops, grips feet

carpet.source: cut-pile carpet on pad: absorbs impacts and liquid (mildew after 24-48 h wet is cleaning's); casters roll about 5x harder than on hard floors. Cushion: 6-12 mm of pile over a 10-11 mm rebond pad compress about 12 mm under a falling cup before the pad bottoms out, at about 3 J under a cup's footprint: a mug or a plate dropped from 1.5 m usually survives, an egg from counter height does not

rug.source: an area rug on a hard floor: thinner padding than wall-to-wall carpet (about 6 mm of pile, no pad, bottoms out at about 1 J)

grass.source: lawn turf: blades, thatch and moist topsoil give 3-5 cm under a small falling item and take about 10 J before it reaches firm ground (playground guidance treats grass as a poor surface for a falling child, whose energy is hundreds of joules): an egg dropped on a thick lawn from waist height often survives, a 10 kg box lands about as on the old 0.3 hardness

soil.source: garden soil and beds: loose dug soil gives about 5 cm

mulch.source: bark mulch: a loose layer several cm deep (CPSC playground handbook: 9 in of wood mulch protects falls of up to 10 ft)

default.source: an unknown hard floor: manipulation's fallbacks (FLOOR_HARDNESS 0.9, FLOOR_SCRATCH 0.5, FLOOR_FRICTION 0.4)

feet.doc: Furniture feet and sliding aids. mu_factor multiplies the floor's mu (capped at 1.0; mu_factor_soft on soft floors), scratch is manipulation's FOOT_SCRATCH. Casters roll (c_rr instead of mu). Material classes not listed use a factor of 1.0 and the default scratch.

felt.source: felt pads roughly halve the friction of wood legs on hard floors

slider.source: PTFE furniture sliders: about 0.1 on hard floors; on carpet the pile drags (about 0.3)

caster.source: casters roll: the floor's c_rr applies

upholstered_legs.source: upholstered pieces stand on wooden or plastic legs (manipulation foot_material)
